what_its_for: Brivaracetam is used to help control partial-onset seizures (a type of seizure that starts in one part of the brain) in adults and children 1 month of age and older. It belongs to a group of medicines called anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) and works by calming abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
how_to_take: Take brivaracetam exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes as a tablet, an oral liquid solution, or an injection given by a healthcare provider. Swallow tablets whole with or without food. If you are using the liquid, measure your dose carefully using the measuring device provided — do not use a household spoon. The injection is only given in a medical setting. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this could cause more seizures.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your age, weight, and how well your seizures are controlled. The usual starting dose for adults is 50 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening). Your doctor may adjust your dose over time. For children, the dose is based on body weight. Always take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store tablets and oral solution at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the oral solution in the original bottle and do not freeze it. Once opened, the oral solution can be used for up to 5 months. Keep all forms of this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not flush medicines down the toilet or pour them down a drain unless instructed — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking brivaracetam, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may raise your risk of side effects. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness and sleepiness. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: new or worsening depression, anxiety, agitation, or unusual changes in mood or behavior; thoughts of hurting yourself or suicide; severe confusion or aggression; a sudden increase in seizures; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing; or if you feel unusually drowsy or unsteady on your feet. Also tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as some drugs can interact with brivaracetam.
when_it_works: Brivaracetam starts working relatively quickly, and some people may notice fewer seizures within the first few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several weeks for the full benefit to be seen. It is important to keep taking this medicine every day even if you feel well, because stopping suddenly can bring seizures back.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Seizure medicines may cause harm to an unborn baby, but uncontrolled seizures also carry risks. Talk to your doctor about the best option for you. Breastfeeding: It is not known if brivaracetam passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to the dizziness and drowsiness caused by this medicine and should take care to avoid falls. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have liver problems. Let your doctor know about any kidney or liver conditions before starting this medicine.
